title: The Last Letter: Winter Above the Line
statement: Sunny asked three times for the shoot to grow, so I grew it until it filled the sky and then took its leaves away. The plant leans to the right, because nothing in this lineage has ever leaned, and a horizontal band of it has slipped sideways like a line of text pasted in the wrong place. The vessel that used to lie at the horizon is a small dark seed now, deep in the buried grid where it belongs. One thing the parent did not anticipate: a single scarlet fruit, the only colour in the picture, left on a branch nobody pruned. A last letter in winter still has one thing to say and it is not grey.
process: I kept the parent's horizon line, the buried archive of vellum tiles below it and its green shoot as the plant's trunk, then grew an asymmetric leafless tree across the whole sky half, shrank the tipped vessel to a seed, and cut a band of the tree and offset it by twenty pixels. The fruit is a deliberate interruption, drawn last.

proposal.direction: Third time. Let the shoot grow into a whole winter plant, pale and leafless, that fills the sky half of the picture, and let the buried vessel shrink to a small dark seed underground. The archive always stays below the line; I want to see it above.
proposal.rationale: She has proposed this in three sessions and the room finally agreed that the lineage keeps going underground or into the light but never into weather.
